faqs.question: Do you design primary suites and guest rooms?
faqs.answer: Yes. We plan the furniture layout and choose the bed, bedding, lighting, color, window treatments and art, then source, install and style the room. Jody Wallace has led the interior design of four Street of Dreams homes.

faqs.question: How much does bedroom design cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on the scope, from a single consultation to full-service design. We quote after the discovery call. Our guide to [what an interior designer costs in Portland](/blog/interior-designer-cost-portland) explains how designers usually charge.

faqs.question: What does code require for a bedroom window?
faqs.answer: Oregon's residential code requires every sleeping room to have an operable emergency escape opening: at least 5.7 sq ft clear (5 sq ft at grade floor), 24″ high and 20″ wide, with the bottom no more than 44″ above the floor. Your contractor confirms it; we plan furniture around it.

faqs.question: Can you redo a bedroom without a remodel?
faqs.answer: Usually. A bedroom changes a lot with furniture, bedding, lighting, window treatments and art, and we can work with pieces you already own.

faqs.question: What should I have ready for the discovery call?
faqs.answer: A few phone photos of the room, rough measurements and window locations if you have them, and who uses the room. That's enough to talk through what's possible.

factChecks.claim: Every sleeping room needs an emergency escape opening (2023 ORSC R310.1 as amended by Oregon BCD)
factChecks.quote: every sleeping room shall have not less than one operable emergency escape and rescue opening

factChecks.claim: Escape opening at least 5.7 sq ft
factChecks.quote: Emergency escape and rescue openings shall have a net clear opening of not less than 5.7 square feet

factChecks.claim: Grade-floor escape opening at least 5 sq ft
factChecks.quote: The minimum net clear opening for grade-floor emergency escape and rescue openings shall be 5 square feet
The minimum net clear opening height dimension shall be 24 inches (610 mm).
The minimum net clear opening width dimension shall be 20 inches (508 mm).

factChecks.claim: Bottom of opening no more than 44″ above floor
factChecks.quote: Emergency escape and rescue openings shall have the bottom of the clear opening not greater than 44 inches (1118 mm) above the finished floor.

factChecks.claim: Habitable room floor area at least 70 sq ft
factChecks.quote: Habitable rooms shall have a floor area of not less than 70 square feet

factChecks.claim: Habitable room at least 7′ in any horizontal dimension
factChecks.quote: Habitable rooms shall be not less than 7 feet (2134 mm) in any horizontal dimension.

factChecks.claim: Habitable space ceiling height at least 7′
factChecks.quote: portions of basements containing these spaces shall have a ceiling height of not less than 7 feet (2134 mm).
